title: First-level Fourier tail bound
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $g$ be a function from the sign cube $\\{-1,1\\}^{n+1}$ to $\\{\\pm1\\}$, and let $\\delta\\in\\mathbb R$. For every assignment of signs to the coordinates other than coordinate $0$, suppose the absolute value of the mean of the resulting one-coordinate restriction of $g$ is at least $1-\\delta$, and suppose $0\\le 1-\\delta$. Then the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $g$, viewed as a real-valued function, on the singleton sets $\\{1\\},\\ldots,\\{n\\}$ is at most $4\\delta^2\\log_2(2/\\delta)$.
